summary: Flathead NF summit tower, 35-ft steel, moved in 1978 to Stoltz land; a 2022 article describes a likely match in a Whitefish yard; summit has little left.

facts.design: 35-foot steel tower, 12 feet square at the base, with a 6.5-foot-square observation room and four large glass windows (1930 report)
facts.status_note: Summit tower moved in 1978; SummitPost says hardly anything is left on the summit. A 2022 article describes a fully working 40-foot vintage lookout in a Whitefish yard that may be the same tower; it does not name Ingalls

access.note: On Flathead National Forest land; SummitPost gives trailhead directions and calls the climb fairly easy. No closure found in the sources read

events.note: October 9, 1930 newspaper reports completion of the first steel lookout tower in the Blackfeet forest on Ingalls Mountain. Firelookout.com and SummitPost give 1934 instead
Moved to a Stoltz Lumber Co. site about a mile east of a nearby peak (firelookout.com says Whitefish Mtn.; SummitPost says Big Mountain)
The 1978 tower, labeled as moved from Ingalls, was removed to private property three miles southeast of Whitefish
Brush Creek Fire burned Ingalls Mountain badly (SummitPost); the tower had already been moved in 1978
Article describes a fully working 40-foot vintage lookout in a rural Whitefish yard, said to have come from Stoltze land near Big Mountain; not named as Ingalls

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An October 9, 1930 newspaper report says completion; firelookout.com and SummitPost say 1934. The 1930 report is contemporary, so it is used as the event year, but no source explains the 1934 date. Not reconciled.

Firelookout.com says a mile east of Whitefish Mtn.; SummitPost says a mile east of Big Mountain. Both place the Stoltz site about a mile from a peak near Big Mountain and Whitefish; the story gives both.
The 2022 article gives 40 feet for the yard tower; the Ingalls sources give 35 feet. The article does not name Ingalls, so the match is probable, not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.field: location of the Whitefish Mountain tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Whitefish Mountain page header says 3 miles north of Whitefish; its text says the tower was removed to private property 3 miles southeast of Whitefish. The story uses the text.

notes_for_editor: The 1978 tower is described on the Whitefish Mountain page as moved from Ingalls. The 2022 yard tower is a probable match only: the article is unnamed and says 40 feet. SummitPost has typos ('there is anything hardly left'); quotes are verbatim. No staffing records for Ingalls Mountain were found. No photos with a clear licence were found.
